milestones.name: ATC Flight Plan Activated
rules: The Airport CDM Platform is initiated for this flight, and all available information is processed.
The ATC Flight Plan is submitted by the Aircraft Operator and distributed by the IFPS to all involved ATC units.
A check shall be performed to verify the consistency between the ATC Flight Plan, Airport Slot and Airport flight data before the first E-DPI is sent.
The AO must provide correct information before the first E-DPI message to feed Network Operations with consistent SOBT, aircraft registration, and first destination data.
The E-DPI message should not be sent if no or inconsistent information is provided.
The flight is ready not later than 15 minutes after the planned EOBT.
The Operational Status changes to INITIATED.
For an arrival, ELDT and EIBT are updated; for a departure, EOBT and ETOT are updated.
This process is triggered by the first activation of the ATC Flight Plan (earliest EOBT-3 hr), or by new or late submissions of the ATC Flight Plan after cancellation or revised EOBT.

milestones.name: EOBT - 2 hr
rules: Network Operations issues a CTOT at EOBT-2h if the flight is regulated, and sends it to relevant ATS units and the departure aerodrome.
For inbound flights, ELDT is updated based on information provided by the FUM messages, taking into account the actual progress of the flight.
A check shall be performed to verify feasibility of the ATC Flight Plan estimated off block time at EOBT-2 hrs, checking whether AO/GH flight estimates are consistent with the ATC Flight Plan.
At EOBT-2 hrs Network Operations is informed through the first T-DPI message of the updated take off time estimate.
Calculation basis for the TTOT shall take into account EIBT+MTTT+EXOT, if later than EOBT+EXOT.
In the case of manual input of TOBT, this estimate overrides the EIBT+MTTT estimate, hence TTOT equals TOBT+EXOT.
Appropriate fields are marked as REGULATED.
other_concepts: priority of CTOT flights over unregulated flights

milestones.name: Take Off from Outstation
rules: The outstation provides ATOT to the Network Operations and Aircraft Operator, directly available with an accuracy of +/- 1 minute.
If the departure airport is more than 3hrs flying time from the destination, the ATOT is received from either the Network Operations FUM or via the AO/GH.
Using the ATOT an ELDT is calculated using the Estimated Elapsed Time on the FPL.
If the flight is within 3hrs flying time of the destination, Network Operations monitors progress using the ETFMS and sends a FUM that provides updates of the flight's progress.
A check shall be performed to verify feasibility of the ATC Flight Plan at take off from outstation, checking whether AO/GH estimated landing time is consistent with the outbound ATC Flight Plan.
A TTOT tolerance of 5 minutes is respected before Network Operations is informed of the updated TTOT via a T-DPI-t Message.
Calculation basis for the TTOT shall take into account EIBT+MTTT+EXOT.
In case EOBT is later than EIBT+MTTT, TTOT equals EOBT+EXOT.
In the case where TOBT is available, this prediction overrules the EIBT+MTTT estimate, hence TTOT equals TOBT+EXOT.

milestones.name: Local Radar Update
rules: The radar system detects a flight based upon the assigned SSR code when the flight crosses a defined FIR/ATC boundary.
Update of the ELDT can trigger a new TOBT to be entered by the AO/GH, or calculated automatically by the Airport CDM Platform.
Any change to a stand or gate is not preferred after ELDT-30', taking into account the taxi-in time (EXIT).
An estimated in-block time (EIBT) is computed using the ELDT and the estimated taxi-in time.
A check shall be performed to commence the TOBT process and verify feasibility of the ATC Flight Plan given the updated TOBT, checking whether the AO/GH TOBT is consistent with the ATC Flight Plan.
Network Operations is informed when the TTOT changes by more than the agreed TTOT tolerance.

milestones.name: Final Approach
rules: The radar system detects a flight based upon the assigned SSR code and identifies when the flight crosses either a defined range/position or passes/leaves a predetermined level.
Update of the ELDT determines a new TOBT.
A check shall be performed to commence the TOBT process and verify feasibility of the ATC Flight Plan given the updated TOBT, checking whether the AO/GH TOBT is consistent with the ATC Flight Plan.
Network Operations is informed when the TTOT changes by more than the agreed TTOT tolerance.

milestones.name: Landed
rules: ALDT is provided by the ATC system or by ACARS from equipped aircraft, available with an accuracy of +/- 1 minute.
The occurrence of ALDT triggers an update of TOBT and TTOT, updated automatically or inserted manually by the AO/GH, calculated on the basis of the defined turn-round period for the departing flight.
The EIBT is updated according to the ALDT+EXIT.
A check shall be performed to verify feasibility of the ATC Flight Plan given the updated TOBT or ATC Flight Plan, checking whether the AO/GH TOBT is consistent with the ATC Flight Plan.
Network Operations is informed when the TTOT changes by more than the agreed TTOT tolerance.
ELDT changes to ALDT.

milestones.name: In-Block
rules: AIBT is provided by ACARS equipped aircraft, automated docking systems, ATC systems, or by manual input, available with an accuracy of +/- 1 minute.
ACGT is considered to commence at AIBT.

The occurrence of AIBT triggers an update of TOBT and TTOT, updated automatically or inserted manually by the AO/GH, calculated on the basis of the estimated turn-round period for the departing flight.
A check shall be performed to verify feasibility of the ATC Flight Plan given the updated TOBT or ATC Flight Plan, checking whether the AO/GH TOBT is consistent with the ATC Flight Plan.
Network Operations is informed when the TTOT changes by more than the agreed TTOT tolerance.
EIBT changes to AIBT.

milestones.name: Ground Handling Started
rules: The Aircraft Operator/Ground Handler provides ACGT, available with an accuracy of +/- 1 minute.
The occurrence of ACGT triggers an update of TOBT, updated automatically or inserted manually by the AO/GH, calculated on the basis of the estimated turn-round period for the departing flight.
A check shall be performed to verify feasibility of the ATC Flight Plan given the updated TOBT or ATC Flight Plan, checking whether the AO/GH TOBT is consistent with the ATC Flight Plan.
Network Operations is informed when the TTOT changes by more than the agreed TTOT tolerance.
ETTT/TOBT and TTOT are updated.

milestones.name: Final Confirmation of the TOBT
rules: The Aircraft Operator/Ground Handler provides their most accurate TOBT t minutes before EOBT (t a locally agreed parameter).

Following the receipt of the TOBT, the ATC system calculates and provides the Estimated Taxi-Out Time (EXOT) based on the predicted traffic load, gate/stand location, runway in use, and waiting period at the Holding Position.
The flight is introduced into the pre-departure sequence.

A check shall be performed at a predefined local time to confirm TOBT prior to TSAT issue and verify feasibility of the ATC Flight Plan estimates given the updated TOBT, checking whether the AO/GH TOBT is consistent with the ATC Flight Plan.
Network Operations is informed when the TTOT changes by more than the agreed TTOT tolerance.
This process is triggered by a new TOBT or TTOT update; no need to confirm an existing TOBT if it has been manually modified before.

milestones.name: TSAT Issued
rules: ATC issues the TSAT t-minutes before EOBT (t a locally agreed parameter).
All relevant partners are informed of the TSAT that has been allocated to the flight.
Network Operations is informed by a T-DPI-s for non regulated flights.
A check shall be performed to see the number of TOBT updates after TSAT has been issued against a locally defined tolerance.
In case the number of TOBT updates exceeds a threshold, the TOBT input is processed according to local procedure.
TTOT is updated.

milestones.name: Boarding Starts
rules: ASBT is provided automatically from the airport system or by manual input by the Aircraft Operator/Ground Handler, available with an accuracy of +/- 1 minute.
All relevant Airport CDM Partners are informed of the Actual Start Boarding Time (ASBT) when it occurs.
At a certain local time before TOBT, a check shall be performed to check the boarding status, checking whether boarding starts in time to respect TOBT.
The AO/GH is informed in case TOBT needs to be updated.
other_concepts: pre-call to gate via FIDS or public address

milestones.name: Aircraft Ready
rules: The Aircraft Operator/Ground Handler provides ARDT when all doors are closed, boarding bridge removed, and push back vehicle connected, available with an accuracy of +/- 1 minute.
ATC refines the pre-departure sequence.
All relevant Airport CDM Partners are informed of the Actual Ready Time (ARDT) in the Airport CDM Platform and that the aircraft is ready for start up/push-back.
At TOBT + tolerance, the AO/GH is informed that TOBT has passed and the Airport CDM Platform has not yet received ARDT or Ready Status (RDY).
other_concepts: pilot request for start up just before TSAT following coordination with Ground Handler

milestones.name: Start Up Requested
rules: ATC records the Actual Start up Request Time (ASRT), based on pilot request, available with an accuracy of +/- 1 minute.
ATC confirms TSAT to the pilot in order to maintain the aircraft in the pre-departure sequence.
All relevant Airport CDM Partners are informed of the ASRT in the Airport CDM Platform when it occurs.
All relevant Airport CDM Partners are alerted when no start up has been requested inside the locally agreed TSAT tolerance window.
If the start up request is not made by TSAT + tolerance, the AO/GH is informed that no start up has been requested, and should update TOBT.
ATC assures that a regulated flight can respect its CTOT provided the aircraft was ready on time (ARDT).

milestones.name: Start Up Approved
rules: ATC provides the Actual start up Approval Time (ASAT) when the aircraft receives its start up approval, available with an accuracy of +/- 1 minute.
All relevant Airport CDM Partners are informed of the ASAT in the Airport CDM Platform and that the aircraft has received start up approval/push-back clearance when it occurs.
A check shall be performed to see if ASAT is in accordance with TSAT.
All relevant Airport CDM Partners are alerted when no start up has been granted.
In case the start up approval is not granted at TSAT + tolerance, all relevant partners are informed and the flight is re-sequenced.
On receipt of ATC approval, the aircraft starts up, pushes back and starts to taxi.
other_concepts: start up request by flight crew (voice or DCL)
locally defined time around TSAT if Milestone Process 13 is omitted

milestones.name: Off-Block
rules: AOBT is provided by ACARS equipped aircraft, automated docking systems, ATC systems, or by manual input, available with an accuracy of +/- 1 minute.
TTOT is updated considering the EXOT.

All relevant Airport CDM Partners are informed of the Actual Off-Block Time (AOBT) in the Airport CDM Platform and that the aircraft has commenced push-back/taxi from parking position, when it occurs.
AOBT always triggers an A-DPI message to Network Operations, or in the case of remote holding at a defined time prior to TTOT.
After a first A-DPI is sent, a check shall be performed to check TTOT updates against the TTOT tolerance before Network Operations is informed, with a new A-DPI, of the updated TTOT.
AOBT is recorded.

milestones.name: Take Off
rules: ATOT is provided by the ATC system or from ACARS equipped aircraft, available as soon as possible with an accuracy of +/- 1 minute.
FSA and MVT messages are sent.
All relevant Airport CDM Partners are informed about the actual take off.
An airborne message is generated and the flight is removed from the departure sequence.
ATOT is recorded.
